newsitem.title: CHINA: China eases rules on domestic firms' foreign trade.
newsitem.headline: China eases rules on domestic firms' foreign trade.

text.p: China has relaxed restrictions on imports and exports by domestic manufacturers, allowing smaller firms to handle their own foreign trade, the China Securities newspaper said on Wednesday.

The State Economic and Trade Commission and the Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation had issued a circular lowering the minimum export amount needed by manufacturing firms to engage in exports directly, the newspaper said.

The export minimum for makers of mechanical and electronic products would be lowered to $1 million from $2 million, while that for high-tech firms would drop to $500,000 from $1 million, the newspaper said.
The minimum for other firms would be lowered to $1 million from $4 million while large state-owned firms would have the export minimum waived, it said.
The newspaper gave no details of how import business would be affected and Chinese analysts said the new measures appeared to be aimed at boosting exports.
Firms applying to handle their own foreign trading business would not have to make feasibility reports or supply proof of credit or foreign exchange earnings from exports, it said.
Companies that exported at least $10 million a year would be allowed to set up their own independent trading houses to handle related import and export business, it said.
China has restrictions on manufacturing firms conducting their own foreign trade business and forces many to go through state trading houses. -- Beijing Newsroom (8610) 6532-1921
